articleTitle: Analysis techniques for the dynamic behaviour of a multigenerator system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The paper presents a method for analysing the dynamic and transient behaviour of synchronous generators in a multigenerator power system. The method describes the generator as well as the transmission network by their nonlinear two-axis equations, thereby allowing for the effects of shunt and series capacitive network elements. It is completely general and is not only applicable to a predetermined network configuration. The nonlinear equations are linearized in order to carry out an eigenvalue analysis of the system's small signal stability. A computer program has been developed which allows the user simply to specify the network topology, loads and generators of the system. The program then automatically configures the network, sets up all the equations, carries out a load flow solution for steady initial conditions, and calculates the transient response. The results of a two generator case study show the effects of shunt loads and series capacitive elements on the system's response.

articleTitle: Research Paper No. 19: The suppression of subsynchronous resonance with the aid of an auxiliary excitation control signal
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper contains the results of an investigation into the possible suppression of subsynchronous resonance (SSR) instability of the 1 072 MVA nuclear powered turbo-generators to be installed at Koeberg Power Station. The auxiliary excitation control strategy considered in this paper feeds a signal derived from generator speed through a phase advance compensator into the rotary excitation system. The results presented in this paper show that the classical automatic voltage regulator and governor loops are of little use in suppressing subsynchronous resonance, and that the auxiliary excitation control signal is only of limited use. The two main limiting factors are the slow speed of response of the existing conventional exciter and its inadequate ceiling voltage levels.

abstract: The paper shows how an extension of analysis employed to determine the radial stress and unbalanced magnetic pull in induction motors(1) will yield all the torque components as well. Corresponding components of unbalanced magnetic pull and torque are compared in tables listing the useful and undesirable outputs of the motor for single sinusoidal excitation. The supply to the motor is assumed to be perfect while the analysis attempts to set out a basis allowing for imperfections in the motor due to its iron circuit, slotting, phase bands, eccentricity and irregularities in the rotor. articleTitle: Mathematical models for a PWM inverter fed induction motor
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper contains the preliminary results of an investigation into the transient and harmonic behaviour of a three-phase induction motor supplied from a pulse-width-modulated (PWM) voltage source inverter. It evaluates the use of the two-axis theory and the simpler ac equivalent circuit method as two alternative mathematical models to represent the PWM voltage wave and the motor circuits. Results are presented for a case study and they indicate that the two methods yield virtually the same answers for the steady cyclic motor current and torque oscillations. The ac equivalent circuit method has simpler equations and may safely be used by drive designers, but it fails to predict the starting-up transients accurately.
